what_was_tested: A symmetric single-feature online classifier of GUARD-like vs BREACH-like pressure (pooled misclassification, equal cost on both error types), with window/hysteresis/dwell selected by the frozen tie-break.
finding: The full-episode pressure mean separates poles well; a causal trailing window recovers only a weak online signal. Symmetric tick-level error near 37% is therefore expected under this feature, not a failed procedure. The flat calibration surface (50/64 configs inside the 0.02 tie band) is diagnostic that window/hysteresis/dwell are not the bottleneck.

decision.do_not_run: the revised n≈300 dual positive-gain outcome experiment implied by shrinking both-pole oracle gains by (1-e)
decision.reason: That sizing solves the wrong engineering objective. Pole A is already good under fixed 2A/2D and is the integrity/preservation control. Pole B is the repair target. Demanding Delta_A>0 and Delta_B>0, or spending hundreds of seeds to prove a positive A gain for a weak symmetric classifier, is misaligned with the board.
decision.keep_frozen: the symmetric calibration RESULT stands as what it tested; it is not rewritten into an asymmetric claim

supersession.V1_SUCCESS_GATE_dual_positive_gain: RETIRED_FOR_SUCCESSOR_WORK — remains historically valid for the V1 SPEC as written, but no further outcome seed may be spent under that gate
supersession.COMPOSITION_SELECTOR_TWO_FEATURE_AMENDME: SUSPENDED — its kill rule still optimizes symmetric dominant-composition accuracy toward a dual-gain / large-n outcome. That objective is superseded by the asymmetric B-trigger successor before any two-feature pass is executed

claim_boundary: This reading does not authorize PPO, GPU, 6v6, a learned selector, or any outcome episode. It only closes the symmetric-classifier path and points successor work at an A-preserving B-trigger.
